content:
Using the corrected exponent:
\[
T_k=\binom{n}{k}x^{3k/2-n}.
\]
Quadratic terms require
\[
\frac{3k}{2}-n=2 \implies k=\frac{2n+4}{3}.
\]
Thus the sum of quadratic coefficients is
\[
\binom{n}{(2n+4)/3}=64.
\]
The only binomial coefficients equal to \(64\) are \(\binom{64}{1}\) and \(\binom{64}{63}\). These would give
\[
n=-\frac12 \quad \text{or} \quad n=\frac{185}{2},
\]
neither a positive integer. Hence no such positive integer \(n\) exists, so the constant term is undefined.

\[
\boxed{\text{No such expansion exists}}
\]
